entities.summary:
Gohard of Nantes (gohard-of-nantes) was a 9th-century bishop of Nantes, lord of Blain, and saint in the Roman Catholic Church. Born into a Frankish noble family, he became bishop of Nantes in 835 CE and was known for his charitable works and spiritual guidance. Gohard was a key figure in the development of the Benedictine Order in France and played a significant role in the establishment of the Abbey of Saint-Benoît-sur-Loire. He was canonized as a saint in 869 CE and remained a prominent figure in French religious life until his death in 843 CE.

The influence of Gohard of Nantes can be seen in the many monasteries and churches he founded or supported, including the famous Abbaye de Fontenay-l'Abbaye. His legacy as a patron of the arts and a defender of the faith continues to be celebrated in France and beyond. Gohard's life and teachings have inspired countless artists, writers, and musicians, cementing his place as one of the most important figures in French history.

Despite the passing of centuries, Gohard's impact on Western civilization remains profound. His commitment to education, social justice, and spiritual growth continues to inspire people around the world. Gohard's story serves as a powerful reminder of the enduring power of faith, compassion, and community.

The remarkable life and legacy of Gohard of Nantes is a testament to the transformative power of human endeavor. His remarkable achievements and lasting impact on the world have left an indelible mark on history.
